rewrite.title: A20: the deck at the Act 1 boss, boss by boss
rewrite.claim: Which boss a run met matters more than the cards. Hexaghost was beaten 4 times in 17 fights; Slime Boss and The Guardian together were beaten 26 times in 34. Most of the raw gap between cards comes from which boss each deck met. Wild Strike decks won only 3 of 9 boss fights, but 5 of those 9 were Hexaghost fights, all lost. Against Slime Boss or The Guardian, Wild Strike decks won 3 of 4, close to the 23 of 30 for the other decks. Fire Breathing stands out against both kinds of boss. Fire Breathing decks beat Hexaghost 2 times in 3, against 2 in 14 for the other decks. They also won all 5 of their fights against Slime Boss or The Guardian. Clash (10 of 11), Spot Weakness (8 of 9) and Pommel Strike (11 of 13) decks also beat Slime Boss and The Guardian more often than decks without those cards. Spot Weakness decks met Hexaghost only once, and Pommel Strike decks twice, so their good overall records partly reflect easier bosses.
rewrite.subset: Real game, A20, runs 28-90. All run-rule versions and fight-guard settings are pooled. Only runs that reached the Act 1 boss (floor 16) are counted: 51 runs, one boss fight each. The deck is the run's deck during the boss fight, read from the floor-16 combat states, so a card from the boss's own reward isn't counted. Upgraded copies count as the base card. A card created during the fight, such as a random attack, doesn't count. 'Slime Boss/Guardian' pools the fights against Slime Boss (20) and The Guardian (14).
rewrite.n: 51 A20 boss fights, 30 won: Hexaghost 17 (4 won), Slime Boss 20 (15 won), The Guardian 14 (11 won). Card groups are 3-13 fights.

rewrite.unit: % of A20 boss fights won, by boss and by a card in the deck at the boss
rewrite.caveat: This shows correlation, not cause, and the groups are tiny. Most of these rows rest on 3-13 fights, and the Hexaghost rows rest on 3-5 fights. These cards were picked as the high and low ends among about 30 cards found in 5 or more boss decks, so a few of them land high or low by chance. Some gaps that look big in the pooled numbers vanish once the bosses are split. Armaments decks beat Slime Boss and The Guardian 11 times in 14, against 15 in 20 without it. Shrug It Off decks did so 9 times in 12, against 17 in 22. A plausible reason Fire Breathing helps against Hexaghost is that it deals damage whenever a Status card is drawn, and Hexaghost shuffles Burns into the deck. These records don't prove that link. The pooled settings changed the route through the map over time (rules 1-5, with and without the fight guard), so the decks and HP that reached the boss differ between settings too. The deck reading from the combat piles gives the same 9 Wild Strike decks as the master deck. A count of 10 appears only if a Wild Strike created during the fight is counted.

A boss fight counts as won when one of that run's boss fights in fights.jsonl was won. The A20 runs that reached floor 16 are runs 28 through 90: 51 runs with exactly one boss fight each, 30 of them won. By boss: Hexaghost 4 of 17, Slime Boss 15 of 20, The Guardian 11 of 14. The monsters in the combat states match each run's act1_boss. Every card row and every other-deck comparison matches. Fire Breathing: 2 of 3 against Hexaghost (other decks 2 of 14) and 5 of 5 against Slime Boss or The Guardian (other decks 21 of 29). Clash: 10 of 11 against 16 of 23, and 2 of 5 against Hexaghost. Spot Weakness: 8 of 9 against 18 of 25, and 0 of 1 against Hexaghost. Pommel Strike: 11 of 13 against 15 of 21, and 0 of 2 against Hexaghost. Wild Strike: 3 of 4 against 23 of 30, and 0 of 5 against Hexaghost (other decks 4 of 12). The caveat's Armaments (11 of 14 against 15 of 20) and Shrug It Off (9 of 12 against 17 of 22) also match. 32 cards outside the starter deck appear in 5 or more boss decks, consistent with 'about 30'. Every percentage is rounded correctly.

rewrite.title: Ending the turn with energy and a playable card
rewrite.claim: One 84-turn gremlin standoff (run 83, floor 5) is set aside here because it alone gave a quarter of the cases. Without it, the bot at A20 ended 8.9% of its turns with energy left over, and 5.3% with both energy and a card it could afford to play. The leftover card was usually a Strike. Without that fight Havoc almost never shows up (1 case). The rate depends a lot on the enemy. With The Guardian or a lone Acid Slime (L) on the board it was about 17%. With Jaw Worm, Cultist or Hexaghost it was close to 0. A0 is almost the same once its one long stall (run 18, floor 2, a lone Acid Slime (S)) is set aside: 8.8% and 5.2%. With that fight counted, both levels sit at 10.3% energy left and 6.8-6.9% energy plus an affordable card.
rewrite.subset: Real game, A20 (runs 28-90, all run-rule versions pooled). Turn ends come from the game's own states: the last state of a turn before the next turn starts on the same floor. Fights the fallback rule finished are left out, and so is the run 83 floor 5 fight against Mad Gremlin + Shield Gremlin. Each row is the group of monsters still standing at that turn end. The A0 rates (runs 1-27, with and without the run 18 floor 2 fight) are given only in the text, never on the same chart.
rewrite.n: A20: 2,254 turn ends in 568 fights, with 200 ending with energy left and 120 with energy and an affordable card. Counting run 83 floor 5 gives 2,337 turn ends, 241 and 161. A0: 982 turn ends in 265 fights, with 86 and 51. Counting run 18 floor 2 gives 1,009, 104 and 69.

rewrite.unit: % of A20 turn ends with energy left and an affordable playable card
rewrite.caveat: Affordable means the game marked the card as playable and its cost was no more than the energy left. Status cards such as Slimed count (10 cases at A20). The last turn of each fight isn't counted. Holding a card can be the right play, for example to avoid triggering The Guardian's Mode Shift or to keep an Acid Slime (L) above its split threshold. These numbers don't say whether it was, and an enemy's high rate doesn't show that the enemy caused it. Most rows have only 5-27 cases, and the Slaver rate comes mostly from one fight. The A0 rate with run 18 counted is 6.8% or 6.9%, depending on how turn pairs split by a non-combat state are handled.
